messages.text: Camara to drive for Haas again at Las Vegas GP

metadata.summary: Haas have confirmed that Rafael Camara will continue as Oliver Bearman's team-mate for this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix after making his Formula 1 debut last time out in Brazil.
metadata.content: Rafael Camara: Haas keep Brazilian driver as Oliver Bearman's team-mate for Las Vegas GP following home debut | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rafael Camara: Haas keep Brazilian driver as Oliver Bearman's team-mate for Las Vegas GP following home debut Rafael Camara to continue as Esteban Ocon's replacement for Haas in Las Vegas; team yet to confirm who will drive alongside Oliver Bearman in Qatar and Abu Dhabi ; watch the Las Vegas GP on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday Monday 16 November 2026 10:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rafael Camara reacted to making his F1 debut with Haas during Friday's practice sessions in Sao Paulo Haas have confirmed that Rafael Camara will continue as Oliver Bearman's team-mate for this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix after making his Formula 1 debut last time out in Brazil. The American-owned squad have been left with a vacant seat for the final five rounds of the season following a fallout between French driver Esteban Ocon and team boss Ayao Komatsu last month in Mexico. Japanese driver Ryo Hirakawa, who had already featured in first practice in Mexico, drove in the Mexico City Grand Prix, before Camara, who had earlier in October been confirmed as Ocon's replacement at Haas for the 2027 season, was given the opportunity to make his debut at his home race in Sao Paulo. metadata.summary: Toto Wolff says Mercedes could throw their weight behind George Russell over the final three races of the season to help him finish second in the Drivers' Championship.
metadata.content: Toto Wolff says Mercedes could prioritise George Russell over Kimi Antonelli in final races of 2026 F1 season from Las Vegas GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Toto Wolff says Mercedes could prioritise George Russell over Kimi Antonelli in final races of 2026 F1 season from Las Vegas GP Mercedes hoping for a one-two in the Drivers' Championship to go with dual title triumph; Kimi Antonelli already champion but George Russell currently third; watch the Las Vegas GP weekend on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday Monday 16 November 2026 06:08, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes party on the podium after sealing their ninth Constructors' Championship title Toto Wolff says Mercedes could throw their weight behind George Russell over the final three races of the season to help him finish second in the Drivers' Championship. Mercedes have already secured a world championship double this year, with Kimi Antonelli clinching the drivers' title in Mexico before the team wrapped up the constructors' crown a week later in Brazil. But a difficult run of results for Russell since his last win at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in September has seen the Briton slip out of the top two in the Drivers' Championship. He is third, 17 points behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen in second and only one point ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in fourth. Las Vegas GP: UK schedule and how to watch on Sky Sports F1 2026
